items.title: French Student Protests Continue as Government Seeks Way Out of Crisis
items.summary: Mass protests over decrepit schools and absent teachers are in their third week, with more planned. Officials have failed so far to quell a movement drawing many adult supporters.

items.title: How a U.S. Diplomat Suppressed and Altered Reports Critical of Israel
items.summary: A top aide to Ambassador Mike Huckabee skewed information to portray the Netanyahu government in a favorable light, according to multiple officials and documents obtained by The Times.

items.title: 2 Latvians Arrested after Breaching Perimeter of RAF Molesworth, UK Air Base Used by US
items.summary: Counterterrorism police said the men were found inside the perimeter of R.A.F. Molesworth, a base used by the United States, raising concerns about security.

items.title: Russia’s Silence on Possible Plague Outbreak Stokes Fears of a Cover-Up
items.summary: As rumors spread about a possible plague outbreak in Siberia, the Kremlin turned to a familiar playbook: offering little information about potential bad news.

items.title: Warrants to Search Former Prince Andrew’s Properties Were Unlawful, Court Says
items.summary: A judge in London said that a “significant error” had been made in the granting of search warrants in an investigation into Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor.

items.title: Nana Patekar, Indian Actor Who Embodied the Everyman, Dies at 75
items.summary: He brought the intensity of the stage to the screen and was praised for his craft and philanthropy. He was also accused of sexual harassment.

items.title: China Expands Its Military Reach by Building a Base in Laos
items.summary: The new runway in Ban Keun is currently used by only small jets. Neighboring nations are watching warily to see if Beijing expands it for larger aircraft.

items.title: Escalating Assaults on Ukrainian Cities Are Taking an Enormous Toll
items.summary: At least 30 people were killed in a Russian strike on a commuter bus in the country’s east, officials said, a day after an attack on an apartment building far behind the combat zone killed 22.

items.title: Margaret Papandreou, American-Born First Lady of Greece, Dies at 102
items.summary: The wife of Prime Minister Andreas Papandreou, she led reforms in the 1980s that helped legalize abortion and end other legal and social restrictions on women.

items.title: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Airports Prompt Mass Cancellations
items.summary: The Saudi authorities said they intercepted two missiles targeting Riyadh, a day after they said Houthi strikes on airports in the kingdom killed three people.

items.title: Judge Extends Pause on Trump’s Ban Against CNN, MS NOW and Politico
items.summary: The judge overseeing the case said that the pause would extend until next week, and promised to decide whether to further extend it by Tuesday.

items.title: Shifting Eating Habits Have PepsiCo Investors Seeking Operational Changes
items.summary: Even though sales rose in the most recent quarter, the beverage and snack company is under increasing pressure to expand its business in North America, as consumers cut costs and calories.

items.title: Highest Mortgage Rates in 3 Years Chills the Housing Market
items.summary: The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose to 7.4 percent, putting more pressure on Americans struggling to afford to buy a home.

items.title: A.I. Fueled More Resilient Global Growth, W.T.O. Says
items.summary: The World Trade Organization said that the drag on global trade from the war in the Middle East was more than offset by spending on goods related to artificial intelligence.

items.title: France Is Veering Toward a Potential Debt Crisis Amid Protests and Turmoil
items.summary: French bond investors are demanding sharply higher interest rates, a cautionary development for other high-debt countries.

items.title: Oil Prices Jump on Outburst of Violence in the Middle East
items.summary: Attacks on ships around the Strait of Hormuz have continued as a war between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi militia intensified.

items.title: Amex Supersizes Newark Airport Centurion Lounge Before It Even Opens
items.summary: To meet skyrocketing demand, lounge operators like American Express are racing to build bigger, and the Centurion in Newark’s Terminal A will be a giant.

items.title: The Little-Noticed Exception in Trump Accounts
items.summary: Wealthy donors and companies can donate individual stocks to the new investment accounts for millions of children. That has raised legal questions.

items.title: Trump’s White House Ban on CNN, Politico and MS Now: What to Know
items.summary: A judge temporarily blocked the president from barring journalists from White House grounds, but they are being excluded in other ways.

items.title: Can Your College Affect Your Income?
items.summary: A new analysis of federal earnings data measures how much students who received federal financial aid earned four years after graduating. Our graphics reporter Arfa Momin studied the data to see when a graduate’s major and college mattered most to earnings.

items.title: Why My Conversations with OpenAI’s ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ Made Me Very Worried
items.summary: A new mode includes a study tool, but it still does a user’s homework. And a children’s safety nonprofit says the chatbot flunked its tests.

items.title: Clinical Trial Indicates A.I. Chatbots Could Aid Urgent Care
items.summary: Nearly 100 patients discussed their maladies with a Google bot, called AMIE, before meeting with physicians.

items.title: Before Computer Science Became a Boys’ Club, Margaret Hamilton Wrote the Code
items.summary: The woman who helped put astronauts on the moon was a software engineer when the field was not prestigious or lucrative.

items.title: Man vs. ‘Terminator’-Like Robot in a Cage. California Called It Illegal.
items.summary: A tech start-up’s stunt in San Francisco tested the boundaries of combat sport safety and regulations.

items.title: Why A.I. Agents Are Going Rogue
items.summary: Our journalists Sheera Frenkel and Dylan Freedman break down what A.I. agents are, how they differ from chatbots and why A.I. companies are worried about them now.

items.title: A.I. Music Fraudster Who Drew Millions in Royalties Is Sentenced to 18 Months
items.summary: Prosecutors say Michael Smith flooded music-streaming platforms with bots that repeatedly streamed his A.I.-generated music, earning him as much as $8 million.

items.title: Energy Firms Try to Squeeze More Power Out of Old Nuclear Plants
items.summary: It takes a long time to build new nuclear plants. So, some U.S. companies are looking to get more electricity out of reactors that already exist.

items.title: In Race With U.S., China Struggles to Recruit Foreign A.I. Researchers
items.summary: China’s booming artificial intelligence sector has given local researchers good reason to remain in the country, but it has yet to lure overseas scientists despite a government push.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day Is Nostalgic With Rich Visuals
items.summary: In Gears of War: E-Day, it’s fun to see the origins of beloved characters in grand scale, even if its play feels conservative.

items.title: South Korea Investigates Possible Use of A.I. in Hackings on Its Banks
items.summary: The president said there were signs that such models were used in recent attacks on several banks involving customer data. Police are investigating.
